## 1. What was read

**681 research articles** from 32 of the 33 journals on the roster.

A further **174** records (20% of the 855 this month's harvest returned) carry no abstract and are not research: news, correspondence, editor highlights and obituaries. PubMed types them `Journal Article` and nothing else, so the publication-type filter cannot see them — across the whole index they are 22.7% of it and 35% of `general`, and 3,801 of them are JAMA. Every count below is over the full harvest and is inflated by this; the figure above is not.

| General | Cancer | Immune | Bioinfo | Sysbio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 376 | 187 | 80 | 196 | 16 |

!!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: bioinfo -31%, sysbio -33%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months: across the 44 months read, 4 of 33 journals are absent from at least one, worst being *Nat Mach Intell* (20 months missing, 81 papers in total) and *Bioinformatics* (4 months missing, 2,905 papers in total). This month is missing *Nat Mach Intell*. Queried directly, PubMed returns zero for those journal-months too — the holes are in the source, reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest. So a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet, and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: Nature 100, Science 81, Nucleic Acids Res 73, JAMA 53, J Clin Oncol 47, Bioinformatics 43.

## 3. The evidence that moved it


!!! note "Written in arrears, and from titles only"
    2023 was read after 2024, 2025 and 2026, and against titles and journal
    names alone — the 2023 harvest carries no abstracts. Every card is one a
    title will carry unaided; anything a title merely implies was left uncarded.

**The one trial that tests the ctDNA claim directly will not tell a title-only
reader what it found.** [36423745](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36423745/) (*Ann Oncol*) reports the c-TRAK TN trial,
which used ctDNA mutation tracking to detect residual disease and *trigger*
intervention in early-stage triple-negative breast cancer. That is the
`ctdna-mrd` claim built into a protocol rather than inferred from a survival
curve, and it is the only such design in the quarter. The title states the design
and the existence of results and stops there; the card is neutral, and that is a
limit of this month's reading rather than a property of the trial.

**Recurrent neoantigens from splice junctions between exons and transposable
elements, twice in one issue.** [36735774](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36735774/) and [36735776](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36735776/) (*Sci Immunol*)
report the same antigen class from two angles — immunogenic in lung cancer
patients, and epigenetically controlled. The load-bearing word is *recurrent*:
these are shared across patients, which enlarges the target space while removing
the per-patient manufacturing that the thread's own claim assumes is required.

**Engineered cell therapy generalises on two axes at once.** [36690811](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36690811/)
(*Nat Med*) reports interim phase 1 results for an allogeneic, off-the-shelf CAR
against BCMA in relapsed and refractory myeloma. A non-CD19 target and
non-autologous manufacture in the same product is a harder test of the thread
than either would be alone.

**Spatial single-cell tumour atlases arrive back to back in one journal issue.**
[36725934](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36725934/) and [36725935](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36725935/) (*Nature*): the lung tumour immune
microenvironment, and primary and metastatic brain tumours. Two atlases side by
side is spatial multi-omics being handled as an expected deliverable rather than
as a demonstration, which is the modality half of what `single-cell-3d-genome`
claims.

**The neuro-immune-microbiome thread turns `forming` on two mechanisms, not on
volume.** [36693372](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36693372/) (*Immunity*): dopamine reprogrammes ILC2 metabolism and
shuts down the inflammation those cells drive — a neurotransmitter as the direct
control input, which is the thread's shared-currency clause stated as one
experiment. [36640762](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36640762/) (*Cell*): immunity directed at the microbiota is what
permits sensory neurons to regenerate, joining all three arms in a single causal
chain.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

**CD39 is read two incompatible ways inside eight weeks.** [36543958](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36543958/)
(*Nat Immunol*) makes CD39 the suppressive effector of exhausted T cells under
hypoxia — the target-nomination reading, and the one an inhibitor programme needs.
[36792124](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36792124/) (*JITC*), the same month, uses CD39 with CD103 to identify
neoantigen-specific cytotoxic T cells in low-mutation colorectal cancer, and
[36574773](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36574773/) (*Immunity*) in January made it the marker of the tumour-reactive
compartment that predicts checkpoint response. Three papers, two months, one
molecule, and the disagreement is not about effect size but about which side of
the synapse it belongs to. This strains `next-gen-checkpoints` rather than
supporting it: the thread claims that targets beyond PD-1/CTLA-4 deliver a second
generation of blockade, and a nomination whose sign is unsettled in its own
literature is not yet a target.

**Neutrophils invert, with two opposite prescriptions in the same month.**
[36706760](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36706760/) (*Cancer Cell*) proposes neutrophil-*activating* therapy for
cancer. [36800412](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36800412/) (*Sci Immunol*), the same month, reports lung mesenchymal
cells reprogramming neutrophils into an immunosuppressive state that promotes
breast cancer metastasis. Both are defensible readings of the same cell and they
prescribe recruitment and removal respectively. That is a refutation of the
depletion logic itself, not a disagreement about one target.

`suppressive-population-inversion` therefore sits at 0/−4, and the number needs
its denominator before anyone reads a collapse into it. The thread's own
`denominator` field records that its supporting side is a genre rather than a set
of citable findings — the templated preclinical block that nominates a suppressive
population, deletes it, and reverses immune suppression in mice — running at
roughly a dozen to thirty papers a month across the oncology journals and
producing nothing worth a card. A card is written when a population *inverts*. So
an all-refutes column is what the reading rule produces by design, and the honest
statement of it is documented inversions against a steady stream of uncarded
nominations.

[36658434](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36658434/) (*Nat Genet*): NOTCH1 mutations drive clonal expansion in normal
oesophageal epithelium but *impair* tumour growth, with [36702998](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36702998/) reporting
APOBEC mutagenesis as a common process in normal small intestine. `interception`
needs the measurable precursor and the thing worth intercepting to be the same
population; here they are explicitly not, and the expanded clone may be
protective.

**MRD in this month stops at prognosis.** [36130300](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36130300/) (*Blood*) tracks residual
disease through maintenance in 1,280 myeloma patients and states its purpose in
its own title: improved prognostication. [36084320](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36084320/) does the same for CLL at
deeper sensitivity, [36240445](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36240445/) for risk stratification in childhood ALL, and
[36315929](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36315929/) (*JCO*) for FLT3-ITD residual disease in AML. Four reports, four
diseases, one stated endpoint, and not one of them is a treatment decision.
`ctdna-mrd` claims MRD is treatment-guiding and not only prognostic; this month
the literature is doing the other thing, at trial scale, and the single trial
that does otherwise is the one whose result a title cannot give.

Three more land quietly. [36725933](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36725933/) (*Nature*) improves immunomodulatory
antibody potency by *lowering* affinity for the target, putting the gain in the
antibody's format rather than in the choice of receptor. [36702947](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36702947/)
(*Nat Med*) explains durable antitumour immunity by persistent tumour mutation
burden, returning the determinant of response to inside the cancer cell.
[36203013](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36203013/) (*Nat Biotechnol*) reports that post-translational modification
reshapes the presented MHC-I repertoire — the antigens a tumour actually displays
are not recoverable from the genome that every prediction pipeline takes as input.
And [36327160](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36327160/) (*Blood*) reports interventions and outcomes for myeloma
patients needing salvage after a BCMA-directed CAR: the platform reaches the new
indication, and a literature on what to do when it stops working is the shape of
the bound on that.

### (b) Method credibility

`method-credibility` crosses into `crisis` at 0/−5 this month, which is an
artefact of scoring a one-sided ledger by ratio and not a signal about the field.
The objects are what matter.

[36726140](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36726140/) (*Genome Biol*): the collateral activity of RfxCas13d induces
lethality in a knock-in mouse. A widely adopted RNA-targeting effector kills the
animal it is expressed in, which means knockdown phenotypes obtained with it are
not separable from the tool's own toxicity.

[36657438](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36657438/) (*Cell Syst*): genotyping of microbial communities degrades as
reference genome collections grow. The strain-level calls the microbial arm of
`neuro-immune-microbiome-axis` rests on move with the reference rather than with
the biology — and the audit and the thread it undercuts are in the same month.

[36639584](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36639584/) (*Nat Methods*) is carded on `foundation-models` but belongs
here as well: scaled structure prediction returns one structure per sequence, and
[36424442](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36424442/) exists in the same month to add back the ligands and cofactors
it omits. The capability and its stated ceiling are co-present, not sequential.
